rationale: The story is a systemic billing mechanic that accrues on every turn, so it needs an environment, not a product shot or macro strip. Architectural night makes the cost visible as heat: a rack row with every slot mounted and lit after hours says 'every mount bills, all night,' and the blue-hour calm against a wall of amber LEDs carries the quiet expense of default wiring.

core_thesis: Mounting MCP servers the default way re-bills their full tool schemas on every turn — 2x–30x prompt inflation — while retrieving only the few tools a query needs cuts that payload by 99.6%.
core_conflict: The protocol's own strength — many servers, easy to mount — is exactly what multiplies the payload: full-catalog mounting on every turn versus selective retrieval that trims 99.6% of schema tokens but misses the right tool about one query in thirty.
